candidates.exact_span: Results of a groundwater monitoring program developed by a qualified ground-water scientist, or a certification by a qualified groundwater scientist may be used to demonstrate that sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit does not contaminate an aquifer.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Permits either groundwater monitoring results or a scientist certification as the compliance pathway. Interpreting which option applies, or whether both are acceptable substitutes, changes which monitoring obligations were required (B) and whether absent monitoring results can be classified as satisfied by certification, conditional non-requirement, or unresolved missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: A qualified ground water scientist is an individual with a baccalaureate or post graduate degree in the natural sciences or engineering who has sufficient training and experience in groundwater hydrology and related fields, as may be demonstrated by State registration, professional certification or completion of accredited university programs, to make sound professional judgments regarding groundwater monitoring, pollutant fate and transport, and corrective action.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines who may supply groundwater monitoring or certification evidence. Different readings of the qualification criteria change whether submitted certification counts as adequate evidence for monitoring obligations (B) and how missing or disputed certifications are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of monitoring listed in Element II, Section I.D. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Cross-references Element II, Section I.D. to determine applicable monitoring frequency. Resolving which frequency provision applies changes which periodic monitoring requirements were in force for FY2025.

Requires TCLP Pass/Fail reporting on the DMR. Whether Pass/Fail is treated as an enforceable numeric compliance criterion versus report-only monitoring changes limit-exceedance evaluation (A) and whether TCLP monitoring was a binding obligation (B).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/K g) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 5 as well as the applicable pollutant concentration criteria listed in Table 5.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Pairs reported sludge pollutant concentrations with applicable Table 5 concentration criteria. Interpretation of which Table 5 criteria apply, and how mg/Kg values map to enforceable limits, directly determines numeric limit applicability and exceedance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) of PCB's in the sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes PCB concentration reporting in sludge. Whether and how this reported value is compared against an enforceable PCB limit, rather than treated as informational, changes applicable limit determination and exceedance analysis.

candidates.exact_span: Level of pathogen reduction achieved (C lass A or Class B), unless Vector attraction reduction alternative no. 11 is utilized.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a conditional reporting obligation tied to vector attraction alternative 11. Whether alternative 11 applies changes whether pathogen reduction level must be reported/monitored (B) and how absent pathogen data should be classified when the exception may apply (C).

candidates.exact_span: Report No for no liner and leachate collection system at surface disposal site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies a distinct DMR reporting category for sites without liner and leachate collection. Interpreting this report code affects which monitoring/reporting regime applies to unlined sites (B) and whether missing numeric results reflect a documented no-data state versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The certification statement listed in 503.27(a)(1)(ii) or 503.27(a)(2)(ii) as applicable to the permittees sludge disposal activities, shall be attached to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires attachment of a specific 503.27 certification variant based on applicable disposal activity. Which subsection applies, and whether the certification is present, changes evaluated monitoring/documentary obligations (B) and how missing certifications are categorized among documented non-requirement, no-data, or unresolved evidence gaps (C).

Explicitly states that no pollutant limits apply for surface disposal sites with a liner and leachate collection system. Whether a facility falls under this section determines that numeric discharge limit comparison is not applicable rather than unresolved.
